info.title: SyteCheck API
info.description:
The SyteCheck public API runs comprehensive, scored audits of any website —
SEO, accessibility, performance, security headers, and more.

## Authentication

All `/api/v1` routes accept either a session JWT or a personal **API key** via the
`Authorization: Bearer <token>` header. Generate API keys from your account settings
or the `POST /api/v1/keys` endpoint. A getting-started guide, client examples, and an
MCP server live at <https://github.com/BertPC/sytecheck-mcp>.

## Plans and quotas

Every account has a monthly scan quota, a set of analysis categories, and a concurrency
limit set by its plan. **The API itself is available on every plan, including Free** —
an API key confers no allowance of its own, reaching the same quota and the same
categories as the plan it belongs to. Exceeding the
monthly quota returns `429 Too Many Requests` with a `Retry-After` header giving the
time until the calendar month rolls over. Requesting a category your plan does not
include returns `403 Forbidden`. A separate daily burst cap also applies as abuse and
infrastructure protection. Current per-plan limits come from `GET /api/v1/billing/plans`
and `GET /users/me/usage` — do not hard-code them.

## Webhooks

Pass a `webhook_url` when submitting a scan to receive the completed result payload
by HTTP POST as soon as analysis finishes; delivery is retried on failure. Webhooks
require the **Agency** plan — on any other plan the field is refused with `403` and
the scan should be submitted without it, then polled or streamed for completion.

get.description:
Return client configuration needed before signing in, including the IP addresses
our scanners originate from — useful if you need to allow-list them so scans of
your own site are not blocked.

post.description: Create an account and return access and refresh tokens. A verification email is sent; scans require a verified address.
Exchange an email and password for access and refresh tokens.
Exchange a refresh token for a new access token. Refresh tokens rotate on use.
Send a password reset link. Always succeeds, whether or not the address has an account.
Set a new password using the token from a reset link.

Set a password using an invitation token and sign in. The address is already
confirmed, so no separate verification step is needed.

Unknown, expired, and already-used tokens are all refused identically, so this
cannot be used to discover which addresses have accounts.
Confirm an email address using the token from a verification link.
Send a fresh verification link to the account's address.

Begin moving the account to a new email address. Returns `202`: nothing has
changed yet. A confirmation link is sent to the new address and the change is
applied only when that link is used, so a mistyped address cannot lock you out.

Accounts with a password must re-enter it.
Set a new password, re-authenticating with the current one.
Exchange a Google ID token for access and refresh tokens, creating an account if needed.

get.description: Return the authenticated account's profile and preferences.

delete.description:
Permanently erase the account and everything belonging to it: scans, reports,
screenshots, and API keys. This cannot be undone.

Cancel any active subscription first; this answers `409` while one is live.

patch.description:
Update the account's preferences. Email addresses cannot be changed here — use
`POST /auth/change-email`, which confirms the new address first.

get.description:
Return the plan's limits and consumption so far: scans used and remaining this
calendar month, when the quota resets, which categories are available, and any
one-off scan credits.

Quota runs on the calendar month in UTC and does not roll over.

Return the secret used to verify scan webhook deliveries. Unlike an API key it
can be read as often as needed — it verifies that a delivery came from us and
grants no access on its own.

Requires an interactive session and a plan that includes webhooks.

post.description:
Issue a new webhook signing secret. **The previous secret stops working
immediately — there is no overlap window**, so update your receiver first.

Requires an interactive session and a plan that includes webhooks.

get.description:
Return every analysis category with its description and its weight in the
overall score, plus an `included` flag saying whether your plan may run it.

Requesting a category your plan withholds is refused rather than silently
skipped, so check this before passing `categories` to a scan.

Return your scans, newest first, with pagination. Filter by `q` (matches the URL
or label) and by `status`. Deleted scans are excluded.

post.description:
Queue a website scan and return immediately with its id and a `queued` status.

A scan opens a real browser, runs a Lighthouse audit, and has screenshots
reviewed by a vision model, so it takes a few minutes rather than seconds. Poll
`GET /api/v1/scans/{scan_id}`, subscribe to `GET /api/v1/scans/{scan_id}/stream`,
or supply a `webhook_url` to be notified on completion.

**Each scan draws on your monthly quota.** Omit `categories` to run everything
your plan includes; request specific ones with `GET /api/v1/scans/categories`.

Refusals are distinguishable and worth handling separately:

- `403` — your plan does not include a requested category, webhooks, or the
  scan credit you asked to spend. Retrying will not help.
- `422` — the URL or a category id is not valid.
- `429` — monthly quota, concurrent scan limit, or daily burst cap. A
  `Retry-After` header says when to try again.

A scan whose URL turns out to be unreachable is voided before any analysis runs:
it is marked with `quota_refunded_at`, costs no quota, and returns any spent
credit.

get.description:
Return score history grouped by URL for sites you have scanned more than once —
the data behind "is this site improving?". Each URL returns its most recent
points in chronological order.

get.summary: Check for a recent scan of a URL
get.description:
Report whether this URL was scanned very recently, so you can offer the existing
report instead of spending quota on a near-identical one.

Advisory only — it never blocks a scan.

schema.description: The URL about to be scanned.
schema.title: Url

get.description:
Return one scan with its per-category results and screenshot URLs.

Poll this to follow progress: `status` moves `queued` → `scanning` →
`summarizing` → `complete`, or to `failed`. Screenshot URLs are pre-signed and
short-lived — fetch them promptly rather than storing them.

Answers `404` for a scan that does not exist **and** for one belonging to another
account, so scan ids cannot be enumerated.

patch.description:
Update a scan's label. Send `{"label": null}` to clear it. Omitted fields are
left unchanged.

delete.description:
Delete a scan. It disappears from every listing immediately and its stored
results and screenshots are removed permanently after a short grace period.

**Deleting does not restore quota.** A scan that ran has already been paid for.

get.description:
Return the full report: an executive summary with recommended actions, a scored
breakdown, and per-category findings with a recommendation for each.

Available once the scan is finished; answers `409` while it is still running.

Report text is stored in English and translated on demand — pass `?lang=de` or
send an `Accept-Language` header. A translation failure falls back to English
rather than erroring.

Each category carries its own status. `pass`, `warn` and `fail` reflect its
score; `error` means the analysis failed; `blocked` means the site's bot
protection refused automated access. Both `error` and `blocked` carry a null
score and are excluded from the overall score rather than counted as failures.

get.description:
A Server-Sent Events stream emitting a `status` event on each transition and a
final `done` event when the scan finishes.

The connection closes with a `timeout` event after five minutes, so treat this as
a fast path and keep polling as the fallback for long scans.

List your API keys with their scopes and usage counts. Secrets are never
returned. Requires an interactive session.

post.description:
Create an API key for programmatic access. **The secret is returned once, in this
response, and is never retrievable again.**

Requires an interactive session — an API key cannot create further keys.

Choose the narrowest `scopes` that work: `scans:read` alone cannot create or
delete scans, which makes it the safer credential for anything unattended.

delete.description:
Revoke an API key. It stops working immediately and permanently; there is no way
to restore it. Requires an interactive session.

get.description:
Return every plan with its price, monthly scan allowance, included categories,
retention window, and concurrency limit. No authentication required.

This is the authoritative source for plan limits; do not hard-code them.
Return the account's current subscription, plan, and renewal state.

post.description: Begin a checkout for a plan or a one-off scan, returning a transaction to complete in the browser.

get.description: Return links to the payment provider's portal for managing payment methods and invoices.

post.description: Move the subscription to a different plan or billing period.

Cancel the subscription at the end of the current billing period. Access
continues until then, and scan history is kept for a grace period afterwards
rather than being deleted immediately.
Exercise a statutory right of withdrawal on a recent purchase, where one applies.

AcceptInvitationBody.title: AcceptInvitationBody
AcceptInvitationBody.description: Take possession of an admin-created account by setting its first password.

label.title: Label
label.description: Human-readable name to identify this key (e.g. 'CI pipeline').

scopes.title: Scopes
scopes.description: What this key may do: `scans:read`, `scans:write`. Defaults to all of them. A read-only key cannot spend scan quota, which is the safer choice for anything that runs unattended. Scopes never widen what a key can reach: account, billing, and key-management routes are closed to every key.

api_key.title: Api Key
api_key.description: The secret key. Store it now; it is never shown again.

ApiKeyCreatedResponse.title: ApiKeyCreatedResponse
ApiKeyCreatedResponse.description: Returned only by key creation — includes the raw secret, shown once.

ApiKeyListResponse.title: ApiKeyListResponse
ApiKeyListResponse.description: All of the caller's API keys, newest first.

ApiKeyResponse.title: ApiKeyResponse
ApiKeyResponse.description: An API key as shown in listings — never includes the secret value.

CategoryInfo.title: CategoryInfo
CategoryInfo.description: Description of a single analysis category.

CategoryReportResponse.title: CategoryReportResponse
CategoryReportResponse.description: Fully parsed result for one analysis category.

current_password.title: Current Password
current_password.description: The account's current password. Required unless the account signs in with Google and has no password set.

ChangeEmailRequest.title: ChangeEmailRequest
ChangeEmailRequest.description:
Request to move the account to a different email address.

The address is not applied here — a confirmation link is sent to it, and only
clicking that link updates the account (see ``POST /auth/change-email``).

CheckoutRequest.title: CheckoutRequest
CheckoutRequest.description:
What the customer wants to buy.

Either a subscription (`plan` + `period`) or the one-off audit
(`product="one_off_scan"`). Prices are never sent by the client — the server
resolves the Paddle price id from the plan table, so a tampered request buys
nothing unexpected.

CheckoutResponse.title: CheckoutResponse
CheckoutResponse.description:
A Paddle transaction to hand to `Paddle.Checkout.open({ transactionId })`.

The browser gets only this opaque id. The account the payment credits is set
server-side in the transaction's `custom_data`, so it cannot be nominated by
the client.

ExecutiveSummary.title: ExecutiveSummary
ExecutiveSummary.description: Claude-generated plain-English overview and prioritised actions for a scan.

FindingResponse.title: FindingResponse
FindingResponse.description: One finding within a category report.

MetricReport.title: MetricReport
MetricReport.description:
One measured metric within a category report.

Distinct from a finding: a finding is something to fix, a metric is simply
something measured. A category can report metrics with no findings at all —
which is the point, since it lets a clean report still show its working.
Currently only the ``performance`` category populates these (its Core Web
Vitals and timing metrics); other categories send an empty list.

PlanOption.title: PlanOption
PlanOption.description: One buyable plan, for rendering the plan picker.

plan_name.title: Plan Name
plan_name.description: Display name of the plan, e.g. "Pro".

scans_used.title: Scans Used
scans_used.description: Scans created in the current calendar month (UTC).

scans_limit.title: Scans Limit
scans_limit.description: Scans the plan permits per calendar month.

scans_remaining.title: Scans Remaining
scans_remaining.description: Scans left before the monthly cap is reached.

period_start.title: Period Start
period_start.description: First instant of the current quota month (UTC).

categories.title: Categories
categories.description: Analysis categories this plan may run.

pdf_export.title: Pdf Export
pdf_export.description: Whether PDF report download is included.

public_api.title: Public Api
public_api.description: Whether API keys may be minted and used.

webhooks.title: Webhooks
webhooks.description: Whether a scan may request webhook delivery.

retention_days.title: Retention Days
retention_days.description: How long completed scans are kept.

scan_credits.title: Scan Credits
scan_credits.description: Unspent one-off scan credits. Each buys a single all-category scan outside the monthly quota, and is only spent on explicit request.

retention_grace_until.title: Retention Grace Until
retention_grace_until.description: When the extended retention granted after a plan downgrade ends. Until then scans are kept as though the account were still on its previous plan; after it, `retention_days` applies and older scans may be permanently deleted. Null when no grace period is running.

PlanUsageResponse.title: PlanUsageResponse
PlanUsageResponse.description:
The caller's plan entitlements and their usage against them (Phase 11 B3).

Exists because the limits were previously invisible: a user only discovered
the monthly cap by being 429'd. The SPA reads this to show remaining scans,
label the categories a plan withholds, and decide whether to offer an
upgrade prompt.

PortalResponse.title: PortalResponse
PortalResponse.description:
Short-lived authenticated links into Paddle's customer portal.

Minted per request and never stored — the token appended to each link is
temporary by design.

PublicConfigResponse.title: PublicConfigResponse
PublicConfigResponse.description: Runtime config the web UI reads on load.

PublicPlan.title: PublicPlan
PublicPlan.description:
One plan as the public pricing page renders it.

Deliberately a separate shape from :class:`PlanOption` rather than a loosened
one. That model serves the authenticated plan picker, where every entry is
buyable and every price is therefore non-null; this one has to carry **Free**,
which is the price anchor the pricing page is built around.

It also carries the Paddle price ids, which `PlanOption` has no reason to.
They are not secrets — a price id is a catalog pointer, and the client token
that dereferences it already ships via ``GET /api/v1/config`` — but they are
*configuration* (they differ between the sandbox and production catalogs),
which is why they come from the server rather than a `VITE_` build variable.
The browser needs them to ask Paddle for a localized, tax-inclusive price.

one_off_scan_paddle_price_id.title: One Off Scan Paddle Price Id

PublicPlansResponse.title: PublicPlansResponse
PublicPlansResponse.description: The full plan matrix, for the unauthenticated pricing page.

RecentDuplicateResponse.title: RecentDuplicateResponse
RecentDuplicateResponse.description:
Result of the pre-submit recent-duplicate check for GET /scans/recent-duplicate.

Advisory only — reports whether the caller scanned the same website within the
warning window so the UI can caution against tripping the site's WAF. It never
blocks submission.

categories.title: Categories
categories.description: Analysis categories to run. Omit to run every category included in your plan. Valid values: "html", "seo", "links", "visual", "ai_visibility", "accessibility", "performance", "security_headers", "responsive", "content_freshness".

webhook_url.title: Webhook Url
webhook_url.description: Optional URL to receive a POST with the completed scan payload once analysis finishes. Delivery is retried on failure.

use_scan_credit.title: Use Scan Credit
use_scan_credit.description: Spend one purchased scan credit on this scan instead of your monthly quota. Runs every analysis category regardless of your plan. Credits are never spent unless you set this.

ScanDetailResponse.title: ScanDetailResponse
ScanDetailResponse.description: Scan detail — includes per-category results, score breakdown, and screenshots.

ScanListResponse.title: ScanListResponse
ScanListResponse.description: Paginated scan history for the authenticated user.

ScanReportResponse.title: ScanReportResponse
ScanReportResponse.description: Full structured report for a completed scan, suitable for rendering or PDF export.

ScanResponse.title: ScanResponse
ScanResponse.description: Scan summary — returned by POST and in the scan history list.

ScanResultResponse.title: ScanResultResponse
ScanResultResponse.description: One category's result inside a scan detail response.

ScanUpdate.title: ScanUpdate
ScanUpdate.description: Body for PATCH /api/v1/scans/:id — currently only the label is editable.

ScoreBreakdownItem.title: ScoreBreakdownItem
ScoreBreakdownItem.description: Score and weight for one analysis category.

ScreenshotResponse.title: ScreenshotResponse
ScreenshotResponse.description: One screenshot entry — storage key plus an optional pre-signed URL.

SubscriptionChangeRequest.title: SubscriptionChangeRequest
SubscriptionChangeRequest.description: Move an existing subscription to a different plan or billing period.

SubscriptionResponse.title: SubscriptionResponse
SubscriptionResponse.description: The caller's billing state, for the account billing page.

TrendPoint.title: TrendPoint
TrendPoint.description: One point in a URL's score history.

TrendsResponse.title: TrendsResponse
TrendsResponse.description: Per-URL score history for the authenticated user's completed scans.

UrlTrend.title: UrlTrend
UrlTrend.description: Overall-score history for a single URL the user has scanned.

default_categories.title: Default Categories
default_categories.description: Analysis categories run by default when none are specified in a scan request. Valid values: "html", "seo", "links", "visual", "ai_visibility", "accessibility", "performance", "security_headers", "responsive", "content_freshness".

default_breakpoints.title: Default Breakpoints
default_breakpoints.description: Screenshot breakpoints used by default. Valid values: "mobile" (375 px), "tablet" (768 px), "desktop" (1440 px).

email_notifications.title: Email Notifications
email_notifications.description: Send an email when a scan completes.

dark_mode.title: Dark Mode
dark_mode.description: Use the dark colour scheme in the web UI.

onboarding_dismissed.title: Onboarding Dismissed
onboarding_dismissed.description: Whether the user has dismissed the first-login onboarding walkthrough.

email.title: Email
email.description: Deprecated and rejected with 400. Changing an email address requires confirming the new one is reachable, so it goes through POST /auth/change-email instead.

secret.title: Secret
secret.description: The signing secret, as `whsec_<hex>`. Configure it in the receiver that verifies the `X-SyteCheck-Signature` header.

version.title: Version
version.description: Rotation counter. Rotating issues a new secret and immediately invalidates the previous one, so update the receiver first.

signature_max_age_seconds.title: Signature Max Age Seconds
signature_max_age_seconds.description: How old a signed timestamp may be before a receiver should reject the delivery as a replay.

WebhookSecretResponse.title: WebhookSecretResponse
WebhookSecretResponse.description:
An account's outbound webhook signing secret.

Returned in full on every read, unlike an API key, and the difference is
deliberate. A key is a *bearer* credential — anyone holding it can act as the
account, so it is stored hashed and shown once. This secret grants no access
to anything: it only lets the holder verify that a delivery came from us. The
cost of showing it again is therefore low, and the cost of *not* showing it is
high — a customer who loses it would otherwise have to rotate, breaking a
working integration to recover a value we can simply re-derive.
